# MEMORANDUM

**To:** Supervising Partner
**From:** [Associate]
**Date:** November 20, 2026
**Re:** Naigert Filtration Systems, Inc. / Steinaix Industrial Fabrics, LLC: issue-spotting review of the supply arrangement
**Privileged & Confidential: Attorney Work Product**

---

## 1. Summary

I reviewed all eight documents in the folder:

- the Supply Agreement dated April 1, 2024 (the "SA");
- Statement of Work No. 1 (the "SOW");
- Naigert's October 14, 2026 non-renewal letter;
- the Data Processing Addendum dated June 3, 2024 (the "DPA");
- the Parent Guaranty from Steinaix Holdings, Inc.;
- Amendment No. 1 dated July 15, 2025;
- Steinaix's September 22, 2025 press release; and
- Steinaix's April 2, 2026 certificate of insurance.

I found six substantive issues. The most urgent is that **Naigert's non-renewal notice appears to have been sent late.** If it was, Steinaix can hold Naigert to a two-year renewal through **March 31, 2029**. That renewal would carry an exclusivity obligation that reaches Naigert's entire worldwide industrial-fabric spend.

Several other provisions shift risk heavily onto Naigert:

- Naigert's End Product indemnity is uncapped, while Steinaix's indemnity is capped.
- The Mexican affiliate's obligations are not guaranteed.
- The DPA quietly re-caps Steinaix's data-breach liability.
- Steinaix may assign the contract to anyone, including a Naigert competitor.

**Key background terms:**

| Term | Provision |
|---|---|
| Liability cap | Each party's total liability is capped at **the fees paid or payable by Naigert in the 12 months preceding the claim** (SA §12.1). The carve-outs in §12.3 cover (a) fraud, gross negligence and willful misconduct; (b) Naigert's §11.2 indemnity; and (c) Steinaix's breach of §14. |
| Parent guarantor | **Steinaix Holdings, Inc.**, a Delaware corporation, guarantees "Supplier's" obligations under the Parent Guaranty delivered under SA §20.3. |
| Term | The Initial Term is 3 years from April 1, 2024 (ending March 31, 2027). The SA then auto-renews for 2-year Renewal Terms unless a party gives non-renewal notice at least 6 months before the term ends (SA §§2.1–2.2). |
| Order of precedence | (a) Amendments; (b) the DPA, as to Personal Data Processing; (c) the SA body; (d) the SOW (SA §20.4). |
| Governing law / forum | Delaware law; exclusive jurisdiction in the Wilmington, Delaware courts (SA §§20.1–20.2). |

## 2. Issues in Priority Order

### Priority 1 (URGENT): Non-renewal notice missed the deadline; the agreement has likely auto-renewed to March 31, 2029

**Where:**
- SA §2.1: Initial Term of three years from the April 1, 2024 Effective Date.
- SA §2.2: automatic two-year renewal unless notice is given "at least six (6) months before the end of the then-current term."
- Notice letter, ¶1, dated **October 14, 2026**: "hereby gives notice of non-renewal… effective March 31, 2027."

**Analysis:**
- The Initial Term ends **March 31, 2027**, so the last day for non-renewal notice was **September 30, 2026**.
- Naigert's letter is dated **October 14, 2026**, about two weeks late. Under SA §19.3, notice is effective only on receipt. The letter went by overnight courier, so it was received around October 15, which makes it later still. The email copy does not count as notice under §19.1.
- Each document looks fine on its own. The problem only appears when the deadline is computed from the SA and compared with the letter's date.

**Why it matters:**
- Steinaix can take the position that the SA renewed automatically for a Renewal Term running **April 1, 2027 through March 31, 2029**.
- That renewal would carry the exclusivity in Priority 2. SOW No. 1 runs for the Term of the Agreement (SOW §2.1), so it would continue as well.
- Naigert's letter states its belief that the agreement ends March 31, 2027. Naigert may already be planning, or committing to, replacement suppliers, which would expose it to breach-of-exclusivity claims.
- Under SA §20.5, any waiver must be in writing and signed, so Steinaix's silence will not cure the problem.

**Recommended fix:**
1. **Immediately** confirm the actual delivery and receipt date of the letter (courier tracking). Also confirm that no earlier written notice exists.
2. Advise Naigert not to commit to alternative suppliers for post-March 2027 volumes until this is resolved.
3. Approach Steinaix promptly to obtain a **signed written agreement** under §20.5 that either accepts the October 14 notice as effective or terminates the SA by mutual agreement as of March 31, 2027. Naigert's leverage includes the relationship value and the other open points in this memo. Expect Steinaix to ask for something in return.
4. If Steinaix refuses, consider these fallbacks:
   - Review exit rights: §16.1 (material breach with a 30-day cure), §16.2 (insolvency) and §17.3 (force majeure lasting more than 90 days, at the SOW level).
   - Review any conduct by Steinaix that could support waiver or estoppel arguments. Note that §20.5 makes these arguments weak.
   - Use any renewal negotiation to fix Priorities 2 through 6.
5. Docket the next non-renewal deadline, **September 30, 2028** (six months before March 31, 2029). Send that notice by courier well ahead of the deadline and to the correct notice parties. Since Amendment No. 1, those include Steinaix Mexico (Amendment §6).

### Priority 2 (HIGH): Exclusivity covers all of Naigert's industrial fabric purchases worldwide

**Where:**
- SA §3.1: Naigert "shall buy from Supplier all of its requirements for Technical Textiles in the Territory, and shall cause its Affiliates to do the same."
- SA §1.12: "Technical Textiles" means "any woven, nonwoven, knitted or coated industrial fabric," in any form.
- SA §1.13: "Territory" means "throughout the world."

**Why it matters:**
- The commercial deal is narrow. "Products" are the PTFE-membrane needlefelt media and bags listed in the SOW (SA §1.8), and the SOW covers only the three **Covered Facilities**: Cleveland, Louisville and Tulsa (SOW §4.1). The exclusivity is far broader. It reaches every industrial fabric Naigert or any Affiliate buys, at every facility worldwide, including fabrics Steinaix does not make or price under any SOW.
- Naigert is likely already in technical breach for any non-Steinaix fabric purchases, such as cartridge media or fabrics bought by foreign affiliates.
- The only escape valve is §3.3, which applies when Steinaix notifies that it cannot fill a compliant Purchase Order. It does not help for products that have no SOW pricing.
- If Priority 1 results in a renewal, this exposure runs to 2029.

**Recommended fix:**
- Amend §3.1 so exclusivity applies only to (i) the **Products** listed in an SOW, (ii) for delivery to the **Covered Facilities**, and (iii) Naigert itself, without the obligation to cause Affiliates to comply.
- Alternatively, convert the obligation to a percentage-of-requirements commitment.
- Add release rights for price or quality non-competitiveness and for repeated supply failures.
- In the meantime, audit Naigert's current non-Steinaix fabric purchasing to size the exposure.

### Priority 3 (HIGH): Naigert's End Product indemnity is uncapped and covers losses caused by Steinaix's defective media

**Where:**
- SA §11.2: Naigert indemnifies Steinaix for all third-party claims "arising out of or relating to the design, manufacture, marketing, sale or use of End Products, including product liability claims, **whether or not the Products contributed to the Loss**."
- SA §12.3(b): the §12.1 cap and the §12.2 consequential-damages exclusion do not apply to "**Customer's obligations under Section 11.2**."
- SA §11.1: Steinaix's indemnity, including for product defects, has no matching carve-out. It stays capped at 12 months' fees.

**Why it matters:**
- Every Steinaix Product ends up in an End Product (SA §1.5). Suppose a defective Steinaix membrane causes a baghouse failure, emissions exceedance, fire or injury at a customer site. Naigert must then defend and indemnify **Steinaix**, with no cap and including consequential losses.
- Steinaix's own indemnity for the same defect (§11.1(a)) is capped. The two indemnities also overlap, and §11.2 is drafted to win, because it applies "whether or not" the Products contributed.
- This is open-ended exposure for an industrial equipment maker.

**Recommended fix:**
- Revise §11.2 to exclude Losses "to the extent caused by the Products, Supplier's breach of this Agreement, or Supplier's negligence or willful misconduct."
- Delete §12.3(b), so Naigert's indemnity falls under the cap.
- Alternatively, make the carve-out mutual by also excluding Steinaix's §11.1 obligations from the cap.
- Add an express statement that §11.1 prevails over §11.2 for defect-caused losses.

### Priority 4 (HIGH): The Parent Guaranty does not cover the Mexican Supplying Affiliate

**Where:**
- Parent Guaranty §1.1(a): "Supplier" means "**solely Steinaix Industrial Fabrics, LLC**." The Guaranteed Obligations in §1.1(b) are obligations "of Supplier."
- Amendment No. 1, §2: "Supplier" now means the LLC "and **each Supplying Affiliate**." Under §1.15, **Steinaix Textiles Mexico, S. de R.L. de C.V.** is a Supplying Affiliate.
- Amendment No. 1, §§3.1 and 3.3: Steinaix Mexico accepts and performs all Purchase Orders for Coated Products. It also performs the warranty, remedy, indemnity, compliance and insurance obligations for those products.
- Steinaix Holdings did not sign or reaffirm the Amendment.

**Why it matters:**
- The Guaranty covers the SA "as amended" (Recital A), and §3.1(a) lets the parties amend the SA without the Guarantor's consent. Even so, the Guaranty's own definition of "Supplier" is fixed to the LLC alone. On the better reading, the Guaranty does **not** cover Steinaix Mexico's obligations for Coated Products CF-301, CF-302, CB-401 and CB-402.
- Naigert's recourse for defective or undelivered coated media, including warranty, indemnity and safety stock claims, is therefore against a Mexican entity alone. Enforcing a judgment against that entity would be harder and less certain.
- The certificate of insurance names only the LLC as insured and lists only the Gastonia location. I see no evidence that Steinaix Mexico carries the insurance required by SA §15, which Amendment §3.3 makes it responsible for.

**Recommended fix:**
- Obtain a **guaranty amendment, joinder or reaffirmation signed by Steinaix Holdings, Inc.** It should redefine "Supplier" to include each Supplying Affiliate, now and in future, and expressly cover Amendment No. 1.
- Make execution of that instrument a condition of any further Coated Product orders, or of any renewal negotiation.
- Separately, request a certificate of insurance for Steinaix Mexico that names Naigert as additional insured.

### Priority 5 (MEDIUM-HIGH): The DPA pulls data-breach liability back under the cap

**Where:**
- SA §12.3(c): Steinaix's "breach of Section 14" (Confidentiality and Data Security, including Customer Personal Data in §§14.3–14.5) is carved out of the cap.
- DPA §9.1: each party's liability "arising out of or relating to this DPA, including any Security Incident and any breach of Data Protection Laws, is **subject to the limitations set out in Section 12.1 of the Agreement**."
- SA §20.4: the DPA prevails over the SA body "as to Personal Data Processing."

**Why it matters:**
- Read alone, the SA appears to leave Steinaix's data-breach liability uncapped. The later DPA, which takes precedence on Personal Data matters, re-imposes the 12-month fee cap on Security Incidents.
- Steinaix will argue that a breach of Customer Personal Data is capped, which hollows out the §12.3(c) protection.
- The personal data involved is limited to business contact and portal credential data (DPA §4.4), which reduces the practical exposure. Notification, regulatory and remediation costs are still real.
- Steinaix's cyber policy is only $2,000,000, on a claims-made basis.

**Recommended fix:**
- Amend DPA §9.1 to state that it is "subject to Section 12 of the Agreement, including the exclusions in Section 12.3(c)," or delete it.
- Alternatively, amend SA §20.4 so the SA's liability provisions control over the DPA.
- Consider a defined super-cap for data incidents, for example tied to the cyber insurance limit, if Steinaix resists an uncapped position.

### Priority 6 (MEDIUM): Steinaix may assign the agreement to anyone, including a Naigert competitor

**Where:**
- SA §18.2: "Supplier may assign this Agreement, in whole or in part… to any person upon written notice to Customer and **without Customer's consent**."
- SA §18.1: Naigert, by contrast, needs Steinaix's prior written consent to assign.

**Why it matters:**
- Steinaix could transfer the contract, including Naigert's exclusive purchasing commitment, to a competitor of Naigert or to a thinly capitalized entity.
- A transferee could receive Naigert's proprietary Specifications, forecasts and pricing.
- The Parent Guaranty would not follow an assignment to an entity outside the "Supplier" definition, so Naigert could lose credit support altogether.
- The partial-assignment right also allows the contract to be split across entities.
- Naigert has no termination right on any of these events. The Guaranty's §6.2 notice of a change in ownership gives no remedy.

**Recommended fix:**
- Make §18 mutual. Each party would need the other's consent, not to be unreasonably withheld, with a carve-out for assignment to a successor to substantially all of the business.
- Expressly bar assignment to a Naigert competitor and to any assignee that is not covered by the Parent Guaranty or a substitute guaranty acceptable to Naigert.
- Give Naigert a right to terminate, and to be released from exclusivity, on any assignment or change of control of Steinaix.

## 3. Other Observations (Lower Priority)

- **Distractor documents.**
  - The **press release** confirms the corporate structure: Steinaix Holdings is the parent of both operating companies, and Ramos Arizpe makes the coated products. It creates no contractual rights.
  - The **certificate of insurance** states that it "confers no rights." It does show that the CGL ($5M per occurrence, with products and completed operations) and cyber ($2M) limits meet SA §15.1. However, it covers only the LLC, and the cyber policy is claims-made and does not include Naigert as an additional insured.
- **Cap measure.** If a claim arises after the relationship winds down, "fees paid or payable… in the 12 months preceding the claim" could be small. Consider a floor amount.

## 4. Recommended Next Steps

1. **This week:** confirm the delivery date of the notice letter and open discussions with Steinaix on a signed mutual termination or acceptance of the notice (Priority 1).
2. Advise Naigert on its current exclusivity exposure and hold off on alternative-sourcing commitments (Priority 2).
3. Prepare an amendment package covering §§3.1/1.12–1.13, 11.2/12.3(b) and 18.2, DPA §9.1, and a Steinaix Holdings guaranty joinder. Use the renewal and termination discussion as leverage.
4. Docket September 30, 2028 as the next non-renewal deadline.

I am happy to prepare a draft letter to Steinaix and the amendment language.

**MEMORANDUM**

**To:** Supervising Partner
**From:** Associate
**Date:** November 20, 2026
**Re:** Naigert Filtration Systems, Inc. / Steinaix Industrial Fabrics, LLC: Issue-Spotting Review of Supply Arrangement

---

## I. Summary

I reviewed all eight documents in the folder:

1. Supply Agreement dated April 1, 2024 (the "SA")
2. Statement of Work No. 1 (the "SOW")
3. Naigert's October 14, 2026 non-renewal letter
4. Data Processing Addendum dated June 3, 2024 (the "DPA")
5. Parent Guaranty from Steinaix Holdings, Inc. (the "Guaranty")
6. Amendment No. 1 dated July 15, 2025 (the "Amendment")
7. Steinaix press release dated September 22, 2025
8. Certificate of insurance dated April 2, 2026

The press release and the certificate of insurance are background only. Neither creates or changes contractual rights. The certificate says expressly that it "confers no rights upon the certificate holder."

Some baseline terms frame the issues below:

- **Liability cap:** Each party's total liability is capped at the fees paid or payable by Naigert to Steinaix in the 12 months before the claim (SA §12.1).
- **Carve-outs from the cap:** SA §12.3 removes certain matters from the cap, including Steinaix's breach of Section 14 (Confidentiality and Data Security) (SA §12.3(c)).
- **Credit support:** Steinaix Holdings, Inc., a Delaware corporation, is the parent guarantor of Steinaix's obligations (SA §20.3; Guaranty preamble).
- **Order of precedence:** Amendments come first, then the DPA (as to Personal Data Processing), then the SA body, then the SOW (SA §20.4).
- **Governing law:** Delaware (SA §20.1).

I found five significant issues. They are listed below in priority order. The non-renewal problem is the most urgent because it is time-sensitive and may already have locked Naigert in for two more years.

| Priority | Issue | Location | Urgency |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Late non-renewal notice: auto-renewal through March 31, 2029 | SA §§2.1, 2.2; Notice Letter ¶1 | **Urgent: act now** |
| 2 | Worldwide, all-fabric exclusivity | SA §§1.12, 1.13, 3.1 | High |
| 3 | Guaranty does not cover the Mexican Supplying Affiliate | Guaranty §1.1(a); Amendment §2 | High |
| 4 | Steinaix may assign to anyone, including a competitor | SA §18.2 | High |
| 5 | DPA pulls data-breach liability back under the cap | DPA §9.1; SA §§12.3(c), 20.4 | Medium-High |

---

## II. Issues in Priority Order

### Priority 1 (URGENT): Non-Renewal Notice Was Late; Agreement Likely Renewed Through March 31, 2029

**Where:**
- SA §2.1 (Initial Term)
- SA §2.2 (Renewal)
- Non-renewal letter dated October 14, 2026, ¶1

**What the documents say:**
- **Initial Term.** The Initial Term runs three years from the April 1, 2024 Effective Date, so it ends **March 31, 2027** (SA §2.1).
- **Renewal.** Under SA §2.2, the agreement "shall automatically renew" for successive two-year Renewal Terms. Renewal is avoided only by written notice of non-renewal "at least six (6) months before the end of the then-current term."
- **Deadline.** Six months before March 31, 2027 is **September 30, 2026**.
- **The letter.** Naigert's letter is dated **October 14, 2026**, two weeks after the deadline. It states that the agreement will expire "effective March 31, 2027."
- **Notice mechanics.** Notices are effective only on receipt (SA §19.3). The actual delivery date was therefore later still. The email copy does not count as notice (SA §19.1).

**Why it matters:**
- **Steinaix can hold Naigert to a renewal.** On the face of the contract, the letter was untimely. Steinaix can treat the SA as renewed for a two-year Renewal Term through **March 31, 2029**.
- **Exclusivity runs with the term.** The exclusivity obligation in Priority 2 lasts for the whole Term, so it would also bind Naigert through 2029.
- **Operational exposure.** If Naigert relies on the letter and begins moving supply to another source after March 31, 2027, it risks a breach claim.
- **Waiver arguments are weak.** Steinaix has not, as far as the file shows, accepted the notice. SA §20.5 requires waivers to be in writing and signed.

**Recommended fix:**
1. **Confirm the facts now.** Obtain the courier receipt to fix the date of delivery. Find out whether Steinaix has responded or acted in a way that accepts the notice.
2. **Seek written agreement.** Approach Steinaix promptly for a signed written agreement (SA §20.5) that the October 14 letter is accepted as effective non-renewal and that the SA ends March 31, 2027. If Steinaix will not agree, try to negotiate a mutual termination or a shortened tail. Naigert's leverage is the renegotiation of the points below (exclusivity, assignment, guaranty).
3. **Map other exit routes.** Assess Naigert's other rights in case agreement cannot be reached:
   - termination for cause after a cure period (§16.1), if Steinaix has any uncured material breach;
   - insolvency termination (§16.2);
   - force majeure termination of the SOW (§17.3).
4. **Hold off on transition steps.** Naigert should not take irreversible steps to move supply until the term question is settled.
5. **Contain internally.** Calendar the next non-renewal deadline (September 30, 2028) in case the renewal stands. Consider confirming internally how the deadline was missed.

### Priority 2 (HIGH): Exclusivity Covers All Industrial Fabric Worldwide

**Where:**
- SA §1.12 ("Technical Textiles")
- SA §1.13 ("Territory")
- SA §3.1 (Exclusive Purchase)

**What the documents say:**
- **The obligation.** SA §3.1 requires Naigert to buy from Steinaix "all of its requirements for Technical Textiles in the Territory," and to cause its Affiliates to do the same.
- **"Technical Textiles."** This is defined as "any woven, nonwoven, knitted or coated industrial fabric," including in fabricated form. That is far broader than the "Products," which are the PTFE-membrane filter media and bags in the SOW (SA §1.8).
- **"Territory."** This is defined as "throughout the world."
- **Actual scope of supply.** The SOW covers specified items delivered to three U.S. Covered Facilities: Cleveland, Louisville and Tulsa.

**Why it matters:**
- **Breadth.** Naigert and every Affiliate must source every industrial fabric (any filter media, bag, sleeve, membrane or other industrial fabric) at every facility worldwide from Steinaix. This includes fabrics Steinaix does not make or list in any SOW.
- **Breach risk.** Any off-contract fabric purchase anywhere in the group is a potential breach.
- **Lost bargaining power.** Naigert gives up the ability to dual-source or competitively bid.
- **No meaningful safety valve.** The only relief is the order-specific inability-to-supply mechanism in §3.3 and the force majeure provisions.
- **Compounded by the renewal.** If the renewal in Priority 1 stands, this obligation runs through March 31, 2029.

**Recommended fix:**
- **Narrow §3.1** to the Products listed in an executed SOW, purchased for delivery to the Covered Facilities. Consider adding a volume percentage rather than "all requirements."
- **Add carve-outs** for:
  - products Steinaix cannot supply to specification, price or lead time;
  - customer-mandated sources;
  - newly acquired businesses.
- **Add Naigert's right to terminate exclusivity** if Steinaix fails service levels (for example, the 98% on-time delivery target in SOW §8.3).
- **Use this as leverage.** Tie this renegotiation to the Priority 1 discussion.

### Priority 3 (HIGH): Parent Guaranty Does Not Cover Steinaix Textiles Mexico

**Where:**
- Guaranty §1.1(a)
- Amendment No. 1, §2 (also §§1.15, 2.3 and 3.1–3.3)

**What the documents say:**
- **The Guaranty.** Steinaix Holdings guarantees the obligations of "Supplier," which Guaranty §1.1(a) defines as "**solely Steinaix Industrial Fabrics, LLC**."
- **The Amendment.** Amendment No. 1 (July 15, 2025) redefines "Supplier" in the SA to mean the LLC "and each Supplying Affiliate" (§2.1–2.2). It joins Steinaix Textiles Mexico, S. de R.L. de C.V. as a Supplier (§2.3).
- **Allocation of supply.** Steinaix Mexico alone accepts and performs Purchase Orders for Coated Products (CF-301, CF-302, CB-401, CB-402). It performs the warranty, remedy, indemnity, compliance and insurance obligations for those products (§§3.1, 3.3).
- **No sign-off by the guarantor.** Steinaix Holdings did not sign, join or reaffirm the Amendment.

**Why it matters:**
- **The general consent does not close the gap.** Guaranty §3.1(a) permits amendments without the guarantor's consent. But the fixed definition in Guaranty §1.1(a) limits the guaranteed party to the LLC. Steinaix Holdings will argue that its guaranty does not reach Steinaix Mexico's obligations.
- **The unguaranteed obligations.** These include Steinaix Mexico's supply, warranty, indemnity and rebate-credit obligations on the Coated Products.
- **Who Naigert is exposed to.** Naigert's credit exposure on that product line sits with a Mexican operating entity. Enforcing against that entity may be more difficult despite its Delaware forum submission (Amendment §7.3).
- **Insurance gap.** The certificate of insurance names only the LLC as insured and lists only the Gastonia location. That suggests Steinaix Mexico's own insurance compliance under SA §15 has not been evidenced.

**Recommended fix:**
- **Obtain a joinder or reaffirmation.** Steinaix Holdings should sign a reaffirmation or amendment to the Guaranty (Guaranty §9.5 requires a writing signed by the Guarantor and Naigert). It should:
  - redefine "Supplier" to include each Supplying Affiliate under the SA, as amended;
  - expressly guarantee Steinaix Mexico's obligations, retroactive to July 15, 2025.
- **Make it a standing requirement.** Any future Supplying Affiliate designation under Amendment §1.15 should be conditioned on a guarantor joinder.
- **Request insurance evidence.** Ask for certificates of insurance for Steinaix Mexico that meet SA §15.

### Priority 4 (HIGH): Steinaix May Assign to Anyone, Including a Naigert Competitor

**Where:** SA §18.2 (compare §18.1)

**What the documents say:**
- **Naigert's assignment.** Naigert may not assign without Steinaix's prior written consent (§18.1).
- **Steinaix's assignment.** Steinaix "may assign this Agreement, in whole or in part, … to any person upon written notice to Customer and without Customer's consent" (§18.2).
- **No protections.** There is no exclusion for competitors or less creditworthy assignees. Naigert has no termination right on assignment.

**Why it matters:**
- **Competitor risk.** Steinaix could assign the SA to a Naigert competitor in dust collection equipment. Naigert would then be bound by exclusivity to buy all its fabric from a competitor.
- **Exposure of sensitive information.** That competitor would also receive Naigert's pricing, forecasts and proprietary bag designs (SOW §3.3).
- **Credit risk.** Steinaix could assign to a thinly capitalized entity. The Guaranty covers obligations of the LLC "solely." It is therefore doubtful that the guaranty would follow an assignee.
- **Weak notice protection.** The Guaranty's only related protection is a 30-day post-closing notice if Steinaix Holdings ceases to own a majority of the LLC (Guaranty §6.2). It does not stop an assignment of the contract itself.

**Recommended fix:**
- **Make §18 mutual.** Neither party may assign without the other's consent, not to be unreasonably withheld.
- **Allow limited exceptions.** Permit assignment to an affiliate or a successor to substantially all of the business, but:
  - never to a Naigert competitor; and
  - only if the guaranty continues to cover the assignee, or the assignee meets agreed creditworthiness standards.
- **Give Naigert an exit.** Naigert should have the right to terminate the SA, and exclusivity in particular, on any assignment or change of control of the Supplier.

### Priority 5 (MEDIUM-HIGH): DPA Caps Steinaix's Data-Breach Liability Despite the SA Carve-Out

**Where:**
- DPA §9.1
- SA §12.3(c)
- SA §20.4 (order of precedence)

**What the documents say:**
- **The SA carve-out.** SA §12.3(c) takes Steinaix's breach of Section 14 (Confidentiality and Data Security) outside the §12.1 cap and the §12.2 exclusion of consequential damages. Section 14 includes the protection of Customer Personal Data (§§14.3–14.5).
- **The DPA cap.** The DPA was signed later, on June 3, 2024. DPA §9.1 provides that each party's liability "arising out of or relating to this DPA, including any Security Incident and any breach of Data Protection Laws, is subject to the limitations set out in Section 12.1 of the Agreement."
- **Precedence.** Under SA §20.4, the DPA prevails over the SA body "as to Personal Data Processing."

**Why it matters:**
- **The carve-out is likely displaced.** For personal data breaches, the DPA's cap language likely controls. Steinaix's liability would be limited to 12 months' fees, even though the SA appeared to leave it uncapped.
- **Scale of possible losses.** A breach of Steinaix's ordering portal, which holds credentials and log data (DPA §4.4), could produce costs Naigert would bear above the cap. These include notification costs, regulatory fines and penalties, and third-party claims.
- **Insurance does not fill the gap.** Steinaix's cyber coverage is only $2,000,000 per claim and aggregate. Naigert is not an additional insured under that policy.
- **The protection is narrower than it looks.** The SA carve-out appears to protect Naigert, but in practice it now reaches only non-personal Confidential Information.

**Recommended fix:**
- **Amend DPA §9.1** to state that nothing in the DPA limits the SA §12.3 exclusions. Steinaix's liability for Security Incidents and breaches of the DPA or Section 14 should be uncapped, or subject to a separate super-cap acceptable to Naigert.
- **Alternatively, adjust precedence.** Amend SA §20.4 so the SA's liability provisions prevail over the DPA.
- **Strengthen insurance.** Consider requiring higher cyber limits and additional-insured status for Naigert.

---

## III. Other Observations (Lower Priority)

- **Insurance certificate.** The CGL policy shows $5,000,000 limits and Naigert as an additional insured. That is consistent with SA §15.1(a) and §15.2. The certificate itself confers no rights. Request the actual additional-insured endorsements (CG 20 15 / CG 20 26).
- **Press release.** It confirms that Gastonia continues to make the PTFE-membrane products and Ramos Arizpe makes the coated products. Nothing in it changes contractual rights. It does reinforce that a material share of Naigert's supply now comes from the unguaranteed Mexican affiliate (Priority 3).

---

## IV. Recommended Next Steps

1. **This week:** Confirm the delivery date of the non-renewal letter. Open a dialogue with Steinaix to secure written acceptance of non-renewal or a negotiated exit (Priority 1).
2. **Package the remaining fixes** into one amendment request and use it as leverage in the term discussion:
   - narrowed exclusivity (Priority 2);
